title: Воспоминания новичка и приговор врача  (Memories of a Rookie and the Doctor's Verdict)

segments.t: After recalling how Fedya and Senya pranked him on his very first day at Claude Monet, Max's thoughts shift to the hospital. There, the doctor congratulates Viktor Petrovich on his clean MRI scan but forbids him from returning to the kitchen for at least two months.

Две недели у нас, потом домашний режим.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Hey there. Are you the new guy?' Noting how newcomer things are in this beat, Max links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'Yeah. I am Max.' Barinov replies warmly without holding back, making his position completely clear.
'That is Fedya.' Speaking firmly in the exchange, Vika links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'They played the exact same prank on me when I started.' Max steps in boldly in the exchange and chooses "shutili" ("to joke", from the root "shutit") so Vika hears the exact meaning.
'Reporting for duty.' Barinov jumps in steadily with a shrug, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'Viktor Petrovich.' Reacting readily during the talk, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'I have good news for you.' Leaning in frankly around Vika, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Your MRI results just came back.' Barinov steps in evenly without any doubt, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
'You simply cannot take your eyes off them.' Touching on the eyes around Barinov, Vika chooses "glaz" ("of eyes") so Barinov gets the point right away.
'Does that mean I can go back to work?' Returning to the job around Barinov, Max leans on "mozhno" ("it is possible, one may"), which carries the whole predicate in Russian without needing "it is".

'You will have to forget about work for at least two months.' Barinov continues calmly during the talk, without trying to dress up how he really feels.
'What do you mean, for two months?' Underscoring the months on the spot, Vika puts the weight on "mesyatsa" ("months", from "mesyats") as the exchange unfolds.
Две недели у нас, потом домашний режим.
'Two weeks here with us, and then bed rest at home.' Focusing on the weeks in front of Vika, Max reaches for "u nas" ("by us, at our place") to talk about what they share.

That wraps up this scene as max remembers his own first day in the kitchen, while at the hospital the doctor tells Chef Barinov that despite good MRI results he cannot return to work for two months. See you next time!
